newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller says seeks closure of casinos.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller says seeks closure of casinos.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said on Tuesday she was seeking the closure of the country's casinos, increasing pressure on a sector already facing government restrictions.
"I sought the closure of casinos from the interior and tourism ministries," Ciller said after a meeting with economy officials.
It was not clear how much political backing the former prime minister had for her stance on casinos.

Ten days ago Tourism Minister Bahattin Yucel said the government was pushing ahead with plans to reorganise the casino industry, limiting casinos to three designated areas. An island near Istanbul and various tourist resorts are among recommended locations.
In September, the Islamist-led government issued an order to exclude Turks from the country's approximately 70 casinos, but the success of the exclusion order has been limited.
Ciller said that if a new law was necessary to bring about the closure then the matter would go to the cabinet of ministers.
"Casinos do not benefit, they harm Turkey and the work to have them closed has begun," she said in answer to a reporter's question.

She said casinos harmed family life. The Tourism Ministry said in September the ban on Turks gambling had been prompted by moral concerns, heightened by media reports of suicides linked to unpaid gambling debts.
Gaming industry officials protested against the government's plans. They say gambling would continue in illegal underground casinos with no tax benefits to the country or in casinos abroad.
The controversy circulating around Turkey's casinos was fuelled this month by allegations that policemen were involved in the killing of Turkey's "casino king" Omer Lutfu Topal.

The Istanbul police chief and five other security force members were suspended to ease investigation of Topal's murder after Turkey's opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz said police officers were behind his killing.
